item.title: Canada Life adds application status updates to AI assistant
item.description: Canada Life has expanded its AI assistant, CaLi, to let advisors check the status of pending individual insurance applications around the clock. Canada Life introduced CaLi in 2025 to help members register for workplace benefit plans. It later expanded the assistant to answer health and savings benefits questions, before opening it to advisors for process and workflow inquiries in May 2026.

item.title: Liberty Mutual Re explores cyclone data backup
item.description: Liberty Mutual Reinsurance has partnered with Celest.Science to explore a backup methodology for parametric tropical cyclone insurance when key weather data is unavailable or delayed. The companies will investigate whether multiple independent data sources, combined with physical and statistical modelling, can help reconstruct a cyclone’s characteristics when traditional observations are missing. Disruptions to the data used to verify those conditions can complicate or delay payouts.

item.title: State Fund selects Stream for AI claims evidence review
item.description: California’s State Compensation Insurance Fund has selected Stream to help its workers’ compensation claims teams review medical records, correspondence, legal filings and other claims evidence. State Compensation Insurance Fund selected Stream Claims following an evaluation by its claims leadership and technology teams. Stream’s AI platform organizes documents, identifies relevant information and flags inconsistencies.

La integración apunta a sectores como seguros, educación y servicios públicos. item.title: Bayer Wins Roundup Trial as Settlement Decision Looms
item.description: He added that it sends a “strong signal” that plaintiffs pursuing litigation after the Supreme Court decision will “face significant challenges both in demonstrating they have viable claims and putting forth the necessary evidence to prove them in court.” Related: Bayer’s Supreme Court Win in Roundup Case No ‘Silver Bullet’ The key remaining step is a final decision regarding Bayer’s $7.25 billion settlement proposal by a state court judge in Missouri. Related: Bayer Faces Trial Test of Remaining Roundup Claims After Supreme Court Win Bayer shares rose as much as 5.2% in early Friday trading in Frankfurt, extending this year’s gain to nearly 35%. “While another trial win may initially look like business as usual ahead of final approval of Bayer’s proposed settlement, we think this case is more meaningful,” Jefferies analysts including Michael Leuchten wrote in a note.

item.title: Meta Settles With Teen During Trial Testing Claims Social Media Caused Depression, Eating Disorders
item.description: The trial is the second in Los Angeles state court over claims brought by young people who say they became addicted to social media after Meta, Snap, TikTok and Alphabet’s YouTube designed their platforms to encourage compulsive use. Meta Platforms has settled with a teen plaintiff who accused the company of designing Instagram and Facebook to be addictive, causing her mental health problems and disordered eating, attorneys for the plaintiff said on Friday. Social media companies face thousands of lawsuits in federal and state courts by individuals, school districts, municipalities and other government entities alleging the companies knowingly sought to addict children to their platforms, contributing to a youth mental health crisis involving anxiety, depression and suicide.

item.title: King Tides Flood Homes, Businesses Along Both U.S. Coasts
item.description: King tides have inundated parts of both U.S. coasts, flooding streets and sending seawater into homes and businesses in beach communities in California, Florida and the Carolinas. King tides are caused by the gravitational pull and alignments of the Earth, moon, and sun.

item.title: Gone in 20 Minutes: How the Biggest Heist in Crypto History Unfolded
item.description: The bulk of the heist unfolded in about 20 minutes, blockchain records show, beginning shortly after 2000 GMT on Thursday. Hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance, the world’s biggest cryptocurrency exchange, in a record digital asset theft. “In layman’s terms, the attacker may not have stolen the vault key, they may have hijacked the system that tells the vault to release money,” said Joshua Chu, a Hong Kong lawyer who works on crypto cases.

item.title: California’s Coastal Cliffs Retreating at a Rapid Rate: Study
item.description: Researchers from UC San Diego’s Scripps Institution of Oceanography examined high-resolution aerial lidar surveys taken in 2026 and 2023 and found that much of this coastal cliff retreat was concentrated in hotspots in Northern and Central California, and included areas retreating more than 30 feet per year. Researchers estimate 70% of the California coast is made up of coastal cliffs. The researchers findings, published in the International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation, improve the understanding of California’s coastal geology and provide a framework for systematic statewide cliff monitoring.

item.title: Brookmont’s cat bond ETF surpasses $150m AUM. GTS now lead market maker
item.description: Brookmont Capital Management has announced that the Brookmont Catastrophic Bond ETF (ticker ILS), has surpassed $150 million in assets under management as of October 28th, 2026, which comes shortly after the fund transitioned its primary listing from the New York Stock Exchange to the Texas Stock Exchange and secured a lead market maker. In addition, Brookmont also announced that financial technology firm GTS is now the lead market maker for the catastrophe bond fund. As we explained at the time, the key drive behind this move was to expand market maker participation in the catastrophe bond fund, which proved to be a challenge when fund was first launched.

item.title: Cat bond risk spreads may decrease 10% in 2027, but market healthy and growing: Plenum
item.description: Speaking during a recent webinar, executives at Plenum Investments AG outlined that while catastrophe bond risk spreads have tightened around 15% and are expected to decrease around 10% in 2027, cat bonds remain a healthy and very diversifying and attractive asset class. Regarding risk spreads, Hopmann noted the cat bond market is currently in a softening phase. Plenum Investments recently hosted a webinar, where key executives from the firm analysed the current state of the catastrophe bond market and provided an overview of this year’s Atlantic hurricane season.

item.title: Yield normalisation, evolving risk profiles demand structural discipline in ILS: Nickerson, Icosa
item.description: As yields in ILS remain above their historical averages, and underlying risk profiles continue to evolve, maintaining market discipline requires a key focus on instrument format. Moreover, to navigate these shifting investor priorities, Nickerson noted that Icosa draws a clear distinction between what he calls Foundational ILS and Evolving ILS. According to Jordan Nickerson, Co-founder at Icosa Investments AG, navigating the year-end renewals successfully will depend on how effectively ILS managers balance pricing adjustments with contract terms and liquidity.

item.title: Everest advances commercial retail exit with sale of Chile insurance operations to AIG
item.description: These transactions form part of Everest’s strategic exit from commercial retail insurance. Upon completion of the transaction, AIG subsidiaries will acquire Everest Chile’s licensed operations, employees and ongoing insurance business. In March 2026, Everest signed a definitive agreement to sell its Canadian Retail Insurance operations, Everest Insurance Company of Canada, to The Wawanesa Mutual Insurance Company.

item.title: Chubb bolsters its Global Claims team
item.description: Chubb, a global property and casualty insurance company, has appointed Lisa Wilson as Head of North America Claims, Jamie Trish as Global Claims Operations Officer, and Norm Rafsol as Global Claims Technical Director, within its Global Claims team. The trio will report to Kevin Rampe, Senior Vice President, Global Claims Officer, Chubb. She has a proven track record leading teams with service and technical distinction, and I am confident her leadership will help us expand upon Chubb’s legacy of claims excellence.” Trish, in her new role, is responsible for the Global Claims operational infrastructure.

item.title: RiverStone International completes $1.6bn LPT reinsurance transactions with QBE
item.description: Global legacy acquirer RiverStone International has completed its previously announced loss portfolio transfer (LPT) agreements with QBE Insurance Group, representing approximately $1.6 billion in reserves. “Completing these transactions demonstrates RiverStone’s ability to deliver complex legacy solutions at scale. Our global platform, expertise and capital enable us to address portfolios across multiple lines and jurisdictions, creating meaningful certainty for our partners,” said Paul Brockman, Group Chief Executive Officer of RiverStone International.

item.title: Markel Expects to See Runoff Certainty With Enstar’s $1.2B Adverse Development Cover
item.description: Markel Group has entered into a reinsurance runoff agreement with Enstar Group, the legacy acquisition specialist that is providing $1.2 billion of adverse development cover for underwriting years 2025 and prior. “Markel will obtain adverse loss development coverage of $1.2 billion above the $4.8 billion of subject reserves under the transaction terms and pay Enstar a risk premium of $120 million,” Markel continued. Wilson explained that the ADC provides “greater certainty around the runoff” of its Global Reinsurance division and other exited lines such as professional liability and architects and engineers.

item.title: Some Trends Signal Potential Hope for US Commercial Auto: AM Best
item.description: Topics USA Trends Auto Commercial Lines Business Insurance AM Best Chad is National News Editor at Insurance Journal. Commercial auto’s adverse reserve development in 2025 fell to its lowest level of the last 10 years, and there be some momentum as the direct loss ratio for commercial auto was 66.1 for the first half of 2026. The physical damage component of losses in commercial auto recorded a $2.4 billion gain, as insureds “that have been more proactive with fleet monitoring and maintenance have benefited from a reduction in the frequency of preventable accidents, which has likely aided overall auto physical damage profitability,” explained David Blades, associate director of industry research at AM Best.

item.title: Binance’s $6.3 Billion Hack: How Crypto Insurance Works
item.description: Hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance in the world’s biggest crypto heist, putting a spotlight on how cryptocurrency exchanges insure their digital assets against theft and cyberattacks. Read more: Binance Estimates $6.3 Billion Hacked in Crypto’s Biggest-Ever Heist While both crime and demand for protection have tracked cryptocurrencies’ meteoric rise, underwriting such risks remains a niche business offered largely by specialist insurers in the Lloyd’s market and in Bermuda. The global crypto insurance market was valued at $9.37 billion in 2025 and is projected to reach $184.98 billion by 2033, according to Data Bridge Market Research.

item.title: Allianz Ireland offers home insurance quotes through ChatGPT
item.description: Allianz Ireland has introduced a ChatGPT app that helps users obtain home insurance quotes by describing their property and coverage needs. The move follows Allianz’s earlier rollout of Allianz Concierge, a ChatGPT app in Germany that supports insurance inquiries and quotes, including pet insurance. Users can review and confirm the information before submitting it to Allianz.

item.title: Rainier Partners acquires Apex Insurance Services
item.description: Seattle-based private equity firm Rainier Partners has acquired Apex Insurance Services, a Texas-focused non-standard auto MGA platform. Founded in 2014 and headquartered in Richardson, Texas, Apex operates five MGAs: Apollo MGA, Apollo Specialty, Newstar General Agency, Excellent Insurance Services and Ignition Insurance Services. With Rainier’s backing, Apex plans to grow organically in Texas, potentially enter additional states, explore adjacent product categories and acquire other personal lines MGAs.

item.title: AIG to acquire Everest’s Chile business, completes Colombia deal
item.description: AIG has agreed to acquire Everest’s insurance operations in Chile and completed its previously announced acquisition of Everest’s insurance business in Colombia. Everest Chile serves corporate and upper-middle-market clients across property, energy, marine, financial lines and casualty insurance. The acquisition includes its licensed operations, employees and ongoing insurance business.

item.title: GM Paying $220 Million to Settle Allegations It Violated Driver Privacy
item.description: General Motors will pay $220 million to settle allegations that it illegally sold drivers’ private behavior and location data to brokers, who then sold the information to insurers that used it to set and sometimes increase rates. The settlement follows GM’s agreement in May to pay $12.75 million to settle a California investigation into its alleged sale of driver data to two data brokers. GM was accused of pitching Smart Driver to help people improve their personal driving safety, only to violate drivers’ privacy by reneging on its promise not to sell their data without permission.

item.title: South Korean Court Rejects Tesla Owners’ Lawsuit Seeking ‘Full Self-Driving’ Refunds
item.description: A South Korean court on Thursday rejected a lawsuit by dozens of Tesla owners seeking full refunds for money paid for “Full Self-Driving” driver-assistance software, ruling that the automaker had not breached its contractual obligations. In the lawsuit filed in 2024, the owners said: “Tesla Korea has been unable to implement the FSD system option in South Korea for more than eight years since it began selling it around March 2017.” The plaintiffs argued that Tesla had failed to deliver the promised technology, but the court rejected their interpretation of FSD as a system capable of fully autonomous driving, known as Level 5 automation. In China, 10 Tesla car owners have filed a joint lawsuit demanding refunds for FSD and seeking damages equal to three times the purchase price of the FSD option or the entire vehicle, according to a report.

item.title: Toast Sued by FTC For Misleading Customers on Subscriptions
item.description: Federal Trade Commission and a group of eight states sued Toast Inc., alleging the restaurant management and financial technology company falsely told customers they could try its products for free before enrolling them in a subscription that was difficult to cancel. Toast, which had 156,000 customers and $6.1 billion in revenue last year, violated federal and state consumer protection laws, according to the suit filed Thursday in California federal court. In a statement, Toast said it will fight the suit, arguing the FTC improperly used a 2010 law governing certain online subscription practices to target the company’s commercial agreements with restaurant customers.

item.title: Brits nearly twice as likely to spot pressure tactics in horror films as investment red flags
item.description: Investors are almost twice as likely to recognise pressure tactics in a horror film as they are when those tactics are used to promote an investment opportunity, new FCA data suggests. Lucy Castledine, director of consumer investments at the FCA, said : 'Many people can spot a horror movie trap a mile off, but this survey suggests they’re far less likely to recognise the same tactics when they're used to influence investment decisions. But when faced with a ‘last chance to buy’ investment opportunity, only 36% said it would make them more cautious, while 37% said they would feel pressure to buy quickly or risk missing out.

item.title: Sector Snapshot: Travel Tech Funding Heads Toward Multiyear Low Despite AI Push
item.description: The numbers: In the first three quarters of 2026, startups in the travel tech space have raised $2.2 billion globally across just 302 funding rounds, Crunchbase data shows. Travel demand appears to be holding up, but at the same time, investor appetite for travel tech startups has cooled. Even a wave of startups promising to improve travel with AI hasn’t managed to reverse the funding slowdown, a review of Crunchbase data shows.

item.title: The Hartford returns with $280m target for Foundation Re IV 2027-1 cat bond
item.description: The Hartford, a US primary property and casualty insurer, has returned to the catastrophe bond market with an initial target to secure $280 million or more in multi-peril collateralized catastrophe reinsurance protection from the capital markets through sponsorship of a Foundation Re IV Ltd. This latest catastrophe bond from The Hartford will become the eighth transaction is has sponsored since it brought to market the first in the Foundation Re cat bond series of deals back in 2004. Before turning to the new cat bond, the Hartford has $200 million of multi-peril catastrophe reinsurance from the Foundation Re IV 2023-1 issuance that matures around the end of 2026, so it’s good to see this new offering starting at a larger size.

item.title: SafePoint more than doubles Nature Coast Re 2026-2 cat bond target to $600m
item.description: SafePoint Insurance Company is now seeking its largest catastrophe bond sponsorship ever, as the expansive insurance platform has more than doubled the target size to $600 million for its new Nature Coast Re Ltd. This will become SafePoint’s sixth cat bond under the Nature Coast Re special purpose insurer, and its tenth cat bond sponsorship in total. SafePoint’s largest cat bond sponsorship prior to this one was its $250 million Nature Coast Re Ltd.

item.title: SCOR sees competition from broker facilities, third-party capital as opportunity: CEO Léger
item.description: I think that SCOR has very good cards to continue to write profitable business in the year to come.” During the call, Léger was asked for his views on broker-led reinsurance facilities in the market, which the CEO linked together with third-party capital and explained that it’s not necessarily all bad for the reinsurers. Thierry Léger, Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of global reinsurance firm SCOR, explained this morning that while the market is more competitive, with a proliferation of new capital entering, he sees this as an opportunity for the company, while suggesting that if there are better ways to match risk and capital they should be exploited. Our tier one franchise technical expertise across P&C and life and health, and our strategic capital allocation to diversifying and profitable lines of business position us well ahead of the next strategic cycle and to navigate market headwinds.” Later during the call he was asked about how competition shows up in SCOR’s results, on which Léger acknowledged the inevitability that effects will be seen over-time.

item.title: Tokio Marine HCC International and Adrian Flux develop specialist insurance for domestic humanoid robots
item.description: Tokio Marine HCC International (TMHCCI), part of the Tokio Marine HCC group of insurance companies headquartered in Houston, Texas, has joined forces with UK insurance broker Adrian Flux to introduce a specialist household insurance policy for domestic humanoid robots. Like the driverless car policy we launched in 2016, it will be updated as the technology and the risks evolve.” According to Tokio Marine HCC International and Adrian Flux, the policy is believed to be the first worldwide to combine protection for a domestic humanoid robot with cover for the home in which it operates. Tokio Marine HCC International and Adrian Flux say the product has been developed in response to anticipated demand as domestic robotics becomes more widely available.

item.title: Arthur J. Gallagher revenues for 9M’26 soar to $12.6bn
item.description: Patrick Gallagher, Jr., Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, Arthur J. In Q3’26, the core brokerage segment added revenues of $3.5 billion, while the risk management segment added $457 million, compared to $2.9 billion and $402 million in Q3’25, respectively. For 9M’26, the core brokerage arm added revenues of $11.3 billion while the risk management arm contributed $1.3 billion, compared to $9 billion and $1.2 billion in 9M’25, respectively.

item.title: Corgi appoints Bevin as VP, Public Affairs Officer
item.description: Corgi, an AI-native insurance carrier and financial infrastructure company, has announced the appointment of Morgan Bevin as VP, Public Affairs Officer. In her new position, Bevin will leverage her financial services policy and government relations experience help lead Corgi’s government affairs efforts, working at the intersection of insurance, financial services, and emerging technology. Jeremy Eisemann, Chief External Affairs Officer and Deputy General Counsel at Corgi, said: “We’re excited to have Morgan join Corgi as we continue to grow our business and expand our presence across the insurance industry.

item.title: Binance Estimates $6.3 Billion Hacked in Crypto’s Biggest-Ever Heist
item.description: Crypto exchange Binance has suffered a $6.3 billion hack, the largest to hit the digital-asset industry and the latest in a slew of security incidents afflicting the financial sector. Before now, the biggest publicly known crypto hack occurred at exchange Bybit in February 2025, in which attackers made off with almost $1.5 billion in tokens. Binance said in a post on X that about $3 billion of the assets had been frozen on blockchain networks.

item.title: HSBC Seeks to Hedge Data Center Debt With Credit Risk Insurance
item.description: HSBC Holdings Plc is looking to offload credit risk on data center loans to insurers as demand for artificial intelligence-related finance continues to grow. Barclays Plc is looking for insurance on more than $10 billion of AI-infrastructure credit, while Deutsche Bank AG has been working on an SRT tied to about $2 billion in project finance debt, including data center loans. Credit risk insurance, like significant risk transfers, allows banks to mitigate losses and free up regulatory capital that can be used to bid for more business.

item.title: Japan’s Cyberattack Surge Tests Its Push to Strengthen Defenses
item.description: Japan is facing an intense wave of AI-powered cyberattacks that’s laid bare the vulnerability of one of the world’s largest economies to a new breed of hacking. The wave of cyberattacks comes with high stakes because Japan’s industrial conglomerates are key links in the global technology supply chain and the country boasts the world’s second-largest savings pool, all of which are attractive targets for hackers. The crisis is also forcing Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi to accelerate plans to bring Japan’s cybersecurity up to the levels of its peers, part of her agenda of making the nation more resilient to external threats.

item.title: AIA Group reports Q3 2026 VONB of US$1,415m
item.description: AIA Group has reported value of new business (VONB) of US$1,415m for the third quarter of 2026, down 5% at constant exchange rates against exceptionally high prior-year comparatives in Hong Kong and the Chinese Mainland. Lee Yuan Siong, AIA's Group Chief Executive and President, said: "AIA delivered VONB growth of 5 per cent for the first nine months of 2026, despite exceptionally high prior-year sales in Hong Kong and the Chinese Mainland that affected third-quarter growth. VONB from the Group's other reportable segments outside Hong Kong and the Chinese Mainland rose 18%.

item.title: SCOR reports Q3 2026 net income of €206m
item.description: SCOR has reported third-quarter 2026 net income of €206m, down 4.8% from €217m a year earlier, bringing its nine-month net income to €603m. SCOR's Board of Directors met on 29 October 2026, chaired by Fabrice Brégier, to approve the Q3 2026 financial statements. With a solvency ratio of 221%, SCOR is entering the final stretch of Forward 2026 with a strengthened balance sheet as it prepares to unveil its new strategic plan on 3 December." SCOR will unveil its new strategic plan on 3 December, as its Forward 2026 plan comes to an end.

item.title: MS Amlin launches AI wordings tool Wordy Bot for reinsurance contracts
item.description: MS Amlin has launched an AI-powered wordings tool, known internally as Wordy Bot, that analyses reinsurance contracts against its underwriting standards. Wordy Bot identifies missing clauses, wording differences, and potential inconsistencies for review by MS Amlin's underwriters and Wordings team. The tool is already deployed for MS Amlin's North American Property reinsurance book and will support the team during the 1 January renewal season.

item.title: Opterrix Launches AI-Powered Portfolio Management Workflow
item.description: Opterrix (Madison, Wis.) has launched Opterrix Portfolio Management, an AI-powered workflow designed to help P&C insurers analyze portfolio exposures and make underwriting and portfolio-management decisions from a single environment. Opterrix says users can watch the Portfolio Agent run an analysis and take over the workflow at any point. “We want to make that process easier, so insurers can spend less time wrangling data and more time understanding portfolio risk in variable market conditions.” Opterrix Portfolio Management also draws on the company’s existing weather and hazard intelligence capabilities to support event response and ongoing portfolio monitoring.

item.title: Avante Raises $30M to Expand AI Platform for Benefits Teams
item.description: Avante (Seattle) has raised $30 million in Series A funding to expand its AI platform for corporate benefits teams, bringing total funding to $40 million. Avante says the funding will support global expansion and further development of AI agents that help benefits teams analyze programs, evaluate vendors and complete recurring work. “Benefits teams are responsible for one of the largest and most consequential investments their companies make, yet they’re still operating with outdated information, archaic spreadsheets, and technology built for another era,” comments Rohan D’Souza, CEO and Co-Founder, Avante.
